air.hook: Learners already feel air when the wind blows, when they fan themselves, or when they blow up a balloon.
air.summary: In this lesson, learners discover that air is all around them even though they cannot see it. They learn what air is, how we know it is present, and why it is important for people, animals, plants, and daily life.
explanation_paragraphs: Air is the invisible substance all around us. We cannot see air with our eyes, but it is everywhere. We feel it when the wind blows, when a fan cools us, and when we breathe in and out. Air may be invisible, but it is real and very important.

One way we know air exists is that it occupies space. When you blow air into a balloon, the balloon becomes bigger because the air fills it. When you pump air into a bicycle tyre or a football, it becomes firm. This shows that air takes up space.

Moving air is called wind. Wind can move leaves, fly kites, dry clothes, and push boats with sails. Air is also needed for breathing. Human beings and animals need air to stay alive, and plants also need air to grow well.

Air is useful in many parts of everyday life. It helps things burn, helps tyres carry vehicles properly, and helps us keep cool when it moves. So, even though we cannot see air, we can feel it, use it, and observe what it does.
types_or_categories: Still air, which is air that is not moving
Moving air, which we call wind
importance_points: Air is needed for breathing by people and animals
Plants need air to grow well
Air helps tyres, balloons, and balls fill up
Moving air helps cool the body and dry clothes
must_cover: air is all around us even though we cannot see it
air occupies space
moving air is called wind
people, animals, and plants need air to live
simple examples such as balloons, tyres, kites, breathing, and wind
worked_examples: Explain how a balloon becomes bigger when it is filled with air.
Explain how we know air is present when tree leaves move or a kite flies.
real_world_examples: breathing in the classroom or at home
a bicycle tyre filled with air
a balloon used during a birthday celebration
misconceptions: air is not nothing; it is a real substance around us
because we cannot see air does not mean it is absent

parts of speech.hook: Every word in a sentence has a job to do.
parts of speech.summary: This lesson helps learners understand that words do different jobs in a sentence. They learn the main parts of speech in simple language and see how each one helps us speak and write correctly.
explanation_paragraphs: Parts of speech are the different jobs that words do in a sentence. Just as people in a school have different duties, words also have different duties when we speak or write. Some words name people, places, animals, or things. Some words show actions. Some words describe, while others join words or show feeling.

A noun is a naming word, such as boy, school, or mango. A pronoun takes the place of a noun, such as he, she, or they. A verb shows action or state of being, such as run, eat, is, or are. An adjective describes a noun, such as tall boy or red bag. An adverb describes how an action happens, such as quickly or softly.

Prepositions show position or relationship, such as in, on, under, and beside. Conjunctions join words or sentences, such as and, but, and because. Interjections show sudden feelings, such as wow!, oh!, or hurray! These parts of speech help us build correct and meaningful sentences.

Parts of speech are important because they help us speak and write correctly. When we understand the job a word is doing, it becomes easier to form good sentences, read with understanding, and express our ideas clearly.
importance_points: They help us understand the job each word is doing
They make speaking and writing clearer
They help learners build correct sentences
They improve reading comprehension and grammar

transportation.hook: Every day, people and goods move from one place to another.
transportation.summary: In this lesson, learners understand transportation as the movement of people and goods from one place to another. They learn the main types of transportation and why transportation is important in family life, school life, and the community.
explanation_paragraphs: Transportation means moving people, animals, or goods from one place to another. When a child goes to school by bus, a farmer carries food to the market, or a car takes a sick person to the hospital, transportation is taking place.

There are different types of transportation. Land transportation includes cars, buses, bicycles, motorcycles, lorries, and trains. Water transportation includes canoes, boats, ferries, and ships. Air transportation includes aeroplanes and helicopters. Each type of transportation helps people move in different places.

Transportation is important because it helps people travel for school, work, trade, health care, and family visits. It helps farmers take food to the market and helps families buy what they need. Without transportation, movement would be slow and many community activities would become difficult.

Good transportation also saves time and energy. However, people must use transportation safely. We should cross roads carefully, obey traffic rules, enter vehicles properly, and respect transport workers. Transportation is part of our daily life and helps communities stay connected.
types_or_categories: Land transportation, such as cars, buses, bicycles, trains, motorcycles, and lorries
Water transportation, such as canoes, boats, ferries, and ships
Air transportation, such as aeroplanes and helicopters
importance_points: Transportation helps children get to school
Transportation helps workers travel to their jobs
Transportation helps goods move to shops and markets
Transportation helps people reach hospitals, relatives, and important services
Transportation saves time and connects communities
